name: Sun City Girls
label: Drag City
lede: Two half-Lebanese brothers named their band after an Arizona retirement town, played it to punk crowds who threw sandwiches, and stopped for good when drummer Charles Gocher died in 2007.

eras.title: A retirement town lends its name
eras.text: Alan and Richard Bishop spent childhood summers in Saginaw, Michigan, around their grandfather's all-night oud sessions. In Phoenix they started a band and named it for Sun City, the retirees' town nearby. A drummer from California made it a trio, and a trip to Morocco pointed it at the rest of the world.

years.h: Two brothers in Phoenix borrow a retirement town's name
years.p: Alan and Richard Bishop call the band Sun City Girls, after Sun City, Arizona, a planned community for retirees outside Phoenix.
years.xp: Richard Bishop grew up partly in Saginaw, Michigan, where their father ran a surplus store and their grandfather, a master oud player, hosted all-night jam sessions. Alan also played early on with Paris 1942, a group featuring [[Moe Tucker|66742cdb-d1c2-4546-8204-3ff36db12da9]] of [[The Velvet Underground|94b0fb9d-a066-4823-b2ec-af1d324bcfcf]], and briefly with [[JFA|ed1cc87f-1e93-48aa-ad09-e67ccb77be37]].

years.big: "He was the first serious, true jazz musician that I spent any time with."
years.h: A drummer shows up at Alan Bishop's Tempe open mic
years.p: Alan Bishop on [[Charles Gocher|a95e9a40-0be4-4741-b84b-200c3dc67a48]], a Californian who had played guitar in a Prescott acid-rock band called Cha Cha Billy. Gocher turns up at the pizza-parlor open mic Bishop hosts and is made drummer on the spot.
years.xp:
Gocher had been in Arizona since 1971 and later worked at Zia Records in Tempe. He said it took ten years, but he knew he'd meet people he'd feel empathy with.

The lineup never changed again.

years.h: Placebo adds the band to its Amuck compilation
years.p: By the time Placebo finishes its third compilation, only [[JFA|ed1cc87f-1e93-48aa-ad09-e67ccb77be37]] and Sun City Girls have been on all three.

years.h: A Morocco trip, and a shortwave radio to tape
years.p: Richard Bishop stays three weeks, Alan Bishop two months, taping broadcasts and jamming with local players. The tapes come out twenty years later as Sublime Frequencies' Radio Morocco.

eras.title: Sandwiches from the floor
eras.text: Booked into punk shows, Sun City Girls gave the crowds surreal theater, improv comedy and noise. Placebo Records put out the first LPs, and a nationwide tour with JFA confused both audiences.

years.src: Perfect Sound Forever · Phoenix New Times
years.h: A label owner pays for the first album
years.p: Tony Victor of Placebo Records funds the self-titled Sun City Girls LP.

years.h: JFA take Sun City Girls on a nationwide tour
years.p: Phoenix New Times' Placebo oral history calls the pairing odd: skate punks on one side, surreal theater on the other.

years.big: "They absolutely hated us, started throwing things at us."
yt: Who's That Lady, live, New Year's Eve 1985
years.h: Black Flag's crowd throws sandwiches, and Richard Bishop eats them
years.p: Richard Bishop on opening for [[Black Flag|9941a936-196a-4a62-ae53-a69cbc33f20e]]. He picks the sandwiches off the floor and eats them, and by the end skinheads are on stage blowing horns with the band.
years.xp: Bishop told Perfect Sound Forever the band came out with a weird jazz approach to a bunch of skinheads. They didn't stop, and the crowd ended up in the act.

years.h: Grotto of Miracles follows, and Alan Bishop is on staff at Placebo
years.p: The second album, again on Placebo, arrives two years after the debut. Bishop works in the label's office and warehouse.

years.h: Horse Cock Phepner goes after Arizona's governor
years.p: Perfect Sound Forever calls it a filthy look at the Evan Mecham and Ronald Reagan era. It's where Gocher's clear-hair concept first appears.

yt: Trippin' on Krupa, Bohemia Afterdark, Phoenix, 1988
years.h: Torch of the Mystics is taped in a friend's front room
years.p: A borrowed 8-track, a house on Mill Avenue in Tempe across from ASU's Grady Gammage Auditorium. Weeks after the sessions, a car goes through the front window; no one is hurt.
years.xp: Some of the ambient and spoken-word pieces were recorded in the front yard. Richard Bishop played a 1940s Oahu lap steel, and the line hiss had to be cleaned up in the mix.

eras.title: Seattle, and more records than anyone could track
eras.text: Around 1991 the band moved to Seattle and kept releasing at a pace few could follow: LPs on Nick Schultz's Majora label, then their own Abduction imprint, double and triple CDs, and shows where a mop played the horse.

years.h: After the front room, Torch of the Mystics
years.p: Richard Bishop says the band knew it was a powerful release. It became the Sun City Girls album fans hunt for most.

years.h: Sun City Girls leave Arizona for Seattle
years.p: The move comes around 1991. The band later sets up a shared compound in the Ballard neighborhood.

years.h: Dawn of the Devi starts the Majora run
years.p: It's the first of several records for Nick Schultz's Seattle label Majora. Bright Surroundings Dark Beginnings follows in 1993.

years.h: Thirty-five straight shows, and the engineer is a believer
years.p: Scott Colburn starts recording the band at his Gravelvoice Studios. The Stranger says the run converted him to improvisation.

years.h: A mop for a horse, a globe on a pogo stick
years.p: Shows now come with props, bedsheets and a fake campfire among them. Charles Gocher's drums come apart as he plays.
years.xp: Gocher told Seattle Weekly he played drums like Harry Houdini escaping. He called the whole thing an escapist reality.

years.h: 330,003 Crossdressers from Beyond the Rig Veda is a double
years.p: It's one of two double CDs the band puts out that year. The other is Dante's Disneyland Inferno.

years.h: Box of Chameleons runs three discs
years.p: The triple CD arrives the same year Charles Gocher releases his solo album Pint-Sized Spartacus.

eras.title: Radio from everywhere
eras.text: The Bishops' travels became a second project, Sublime Frequencies, a label for radio broadcasts and field recordings from Africa, Asia and the Middle East. Richard started touring solo, and the trio cut what turned out to be its last album.

years.h: The Bishops open Sublime Frequencies with Hisham Mayet
years.p: The Seattle label issues shortwave radio collages and field recordings. Radio Morocco draws on the 1983 trip.

years.cap: Richard Bishop on guitar at Greensboro College, November 2006
years.h: Richard Bishop hits the road alone as Sir Richard Bishop
years.p: [[Sir Richard Bishop|a444f8ff-2f8b-438b-a680-32c1f393244b]] tours Europe, Australia and the U.S. with an acoustic guitar. Drag City signs him in 2007.

yt: Live at the Sky Church, Bumbershoot, September 3, 2004
years.h: Gocher, two years into cancer, records Funeral Mariachi with the Bishops
years.p: The trio cuts what becomes its last album in Seattle. Gocher has told almost no one.

eras.title: No Sun City Girls without Charlie
eras.text: Gocher's death ended the band. The Bishops kept the name off new work, toured his films, and spent the following years putting out the last album and reissuing old ones on Abduction.

years.cap: Alan and Richard Bishop at a Seattle tribute show for Gocher, May 2008
years.h: Charles Gocher dies of cancer in Seattle at 54
years.p: After a three-year fight he kept private, Gocher dies. Alan and Richard Bishop say they won't perform or record as Sun City Girls again.
years.xp:
A private memorial was held at the band's Ballard compound.

Alan Bishop told Seattle Weekly they simply weren't using the name any more, because it couldn't be.

years.cap: Alan and Richard Bishop as Brothers Unconnected, July 2008
years.h: The Bishops tour as the Brothers Unconnected, with Gocher's films
years.p: They cross the U.S. and Canada screening his videos and playing Sun City Girls songs acoustic, some of them his.

years.h: Sun City Girls score Harmony Korine's Mister Lonely
years.p: [[J. Spaceman|e7183895-fe12-4bce-8cdb-bdd8eaa31986]] of [[Spiritualized|65041e06-83d2-4987-ae52-c17a915fc82a]] shares the credit. Drag City issues the soundtrack as DC360.

years.cap: Richard Bishop on stage at the Sunset Tavern in Ballard, Seattle, September 2009
years.h: The last album comes out four years after it was recorded
years.p: Funeral Mariachi appears on Abduction, with [[Eyvind Kang|a4772e12-bda2-4df0-9c3c-8733933865d8]] and Jessika Kenney guesting and a cover of [[Ennio Morricone|a16e47f5-aa54-47fe-87e4-bb8af91a9fdd]]'s Come Maddalena. Pitchfork gives it 7.4.

years.h: Abduction brings Torch of the Mystics back
years.p: Alan Bishop's label reissues the long-sought 1990 album, remastered by Mark Gergis.
